title: Surge propagation causing tokenflow erosion for newly-quantized model builds
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden drops in tokens/sec and elevated TTFT after we rolled out the v2 quantized build for the transformer-xxl family. Initial telemetry shows a cascading backpressure phenomenon: small per-request kernel stalls amplify in high-concurrency routers, causing request batching to fragment and effective token emission to drop by 30–60% for mid-length streams (512–2k tokens). This ticket tracks triage, hotfix, and coordinated rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Restore tokens/sec to within 5% of pre-rollout baseline for 95th-percentile customers under representative concurrency
TTFT 95th percentile reduced to baseline or better on hosted and dedicated pools within the canary window
Backport hotfix and publish rollout plan for Private/VPC customers with step-by-step upgrade guidance
Postmortem describing root cause, monitoring improvements, and an automated regression test merged into CI
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 — Aisha Patel: Customer X (enterprise, Dedicated) reported 40% token/sec drop after scheduled upgrade to transformer-xxl@quant-v2. Escalated to SE + oncall. Attached initial flamegraphs from their dedicated pool.

2026-03-13 10:01 — Diego Marconi: Reproduced locally with synthetic workload (concurrency 18, qps 350). Observed micro-stalls on NVLink transfers when kernel choice switches between int8-fused and fp16 fallback; KV cache flushes coincide with stalls and split microbatches.

2026-03-13 13:28 — Keiko Tanaka (SRE): Deployed temporary rate-smoothing at router (token emission limiter) to reduce amplification. Customers see partial recovery (~15–25% improvement) but throughput still below baseline. Enabled per-customer logging for deeper traces.

2026-03-13 16:45 — Diego Marconi: Experimented with kernel-selector override to force fp16 path on affected instances. This returned tokens/sec to baseline in 3/3 canary hosts at cost of ~8% higher GPU utilization. Draft PR ready: force-kernel-fallback-guard (PR #2418).

2026-03-13 19:03 — PM (Riley Novak): Notifying prioritized customers of mitigation and expected ETA. Agreed to canary the PR to hosted and a single dedicated customer this evening, with rollback plan if error rates increase.

2026-03-14 01:12 — Diego Marconi: Canary deployed to hosted pool region-us-east-1 (subset: transformer-xxl-serving-2). Early telemetry: TTFT 95p back to baseline, tokens/sec recovered to +3% for median. No error-rate regressions observed. Will schedule Dedicated canary at 09:00.
2026-03-14 08:02 — Support (Lila Gomez): Customer communications draft sent. Private deployment customers need an explicit patched package; creating on-prem bundle + upgrade checklist.

2026-03-14 11:37 — Aisha Patel: Postmortem notes: root cause appears to be misaligned buffer stride introduced by quant packer in quant-v2 that created occasional 512B misaligned transfers. At high concurrency these transfers triggered slow paths in the GPU driver producing ~1–3ms micro-stalls that cascade into batch fragmentation. Action items listed below.

2026-03-14 12:05 — Diego Marconi: Next steps: merge PR #2418 (kernel-selector guard) as hotfix, prepare backport to runtime-1.22-stable, publish private install bundle (patch-2418), create CI regression test (simulate misaligned transfer under concurrency), add an alert on 'per-model token-rate deviation > 20% over 5m'.
decision_log: Force kernel-selection to avoid int8-fused path for quant-v2 until packer alignment bug is fixed (approved by SRE and PM)
Do not revert quant-v2 globally — use targeted guard and staged rollout to minimize performance cost for unaffected customers
Prioritize an automated regression test in CI to prevent future misaligned-transfer regressions
